1964.subject: Zoology
1964.text: The given figure shows an angiogram of the coronary blood vessel. Which one of the following statements correctly describes, what is being done ?
options: It is coronary artery which has a cancerous growth that is being removed.
It is coronary artery which is blocked by a plaque and the same is being cracked.
It is coronary vein in which the defective valves are being opened.
It is coronary vein blocked by a parasite (blood fluke) that is being removed.
1964.sol: Angiogram is an X-ray diagnostic procedure used to visualize the blood vessels following injection of a contrast substance into an artery. It is used to image arteries in the brain, heart, kidneys, gastrointestinal tract, aorta, neck (carotids), chest, limbs and pulmonary circuit. Coronary angiography is performed to detect obstruction in the coronary arteries, which can lead to heart attack. It may be performed if you have unstable angina, a typical chest pain, aortic stenosis, or unexplained heart failure.

47277.subject: Biology
47277.text: Identify the correct path of milk secretion by the mammary glands:
options: Alveoli mammary duct ampulla mammary tubule lactiferous ducts
Alveoli mammary tubules mammary duct ampulla lactiferous ducts
Alveoli ampulla mammary duct mammary tubules lactiferous ducts
Alveoli lactiferous ducts mammary duct ampulla mammary tubule
47277.sol: The glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15-20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli. The cells of alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of the alveoli. The alveoli open into mammary tubules. The tubules of each lobe join to form a mammary duct. Several mammary ducts join to form a wider mammary ampulla. The mammary ampulla is connected to the lactiferous duct through which milk is sucked out. The correct sequence of milk secretion is: Alveoli mammary tubules

70998.text: Following are the parts of upper respiratory system i) External nares ii) Nasal cavities iii) Internal nares iv) Nasopharynx v) Larynx vi) Trachea Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
70998.sol: The human respiratory system is anatomically divided into the upper and lower respiratory tracts. The lower respiratory system includes the structures located within or entering the chest cavity, which are the larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and lungs. 71547.subject: Biology
71547.text: Water can easily rise through the conducting elements of xylem due to _____.
options: Water has high surface tension and high adhesive and cohesive force.
Water has high heat of vaporization.
Water has high heat of fusion.
71547.sol: The ascent of sap in the xylem is primarily driven by the physical properties of water, which include cohesion, adhesion, and surface tension. Cohesion is the mutual attraction between water molecules. Adhesion is the attraction of water molecules to polar surfaces, such as the walls of xylem vessels and tracheids. Surface tension allows water molecules to remain together and resist being pulled apart. 77981.subject: Mathematics
77981.text: Three faces of a die are black, two faces are white and one face is red. The die is tossed three times. What is the probability that the colours black, white and red appear in the first, second and third tosses respectively?
77981.sol: Total number of faces on the die is 6 . Number of black faces is 3 . Probability of getting a black face in the first toss is P(B) = 3 6 = 1 2 . Number of white faces is 2 . Probability of getting a white face in the second toss is P(W) = 2 6 = 1 3 . Number of red faces is 1 . Probability of getting a red face in the third toss is P(R) = 1 6 . Since the tosses are independent events, the required probability is the product of the individual probabilities. Required probability = P(B) P(W) P(R) = 1 2 1 3 1 6 = 1 36 .

On the basis of photoperiodic response to flowering, plants have been divided into short day plants (tobacco), long day plant (eg, wheat, hanbane), short-long day plants (eg, Campanula), long-short day plants (eg, Bryophyllum), intermediate plants (eg, wild kidney bean) and day neutral plant

84699.subject: Zoology
84699.text: When both ovaries of rat are removed then which hormone is decreased in blood?
84699.sol: Estrogens are produced primarily by the ovaries. They are released by the follicles on the ovaries and are also secreted by the corpus luteum after the egg has been released from the follicle and from the placenta. Thus, if the ovaries of rat are removed, then the level of estrogen is decreased in blood. Related Theory:- Secretion of progesterone from corpus luteum maintains the endometrium which is necessary for implantation of fertilized ovum and other events of pregnancy.

102418.subject: Physics
102418.text: A simple pendulum has a hollow spherical bob which is completely filled with sand. It is set into small oscillations with an initial time period T₀ . A small hole at the bottom of the bob is opened, and the sand slowly leaks out until the bob is completely empty. Which of the following correctly describes the variation in the time period of the pendulum during this process?
options: The time period remains constant at T₀ throughout the process.
The time period continuously decreases from T₀ as the mass of the bob decreases.
The time period first increases, reaches a maximum, and then decreases back to T₀ .
The time period continuously increases from T₀ until the bob is empty.
102418.sol: The time period of a simple pendulum is given by T = 2 L g , where L is the effective length from the point of suspension to the center of mass of the bob. Initially, the bob is completely filled, so the center of mass is at the geometric center of the sphere. As sand begins to leak, the center of mass of the remaining sand-bob system shifts downwards. This increases the effective length L , causing the time period T to increase. When the bob is more than half empty, the center of mass starts shifting back upwards.

121354.sol: Commonly known forms of basidiomycetes are mushrooms, bracket fungi or puffballs. They grow in soil, on logs and tree stumps and in living plant bodies as parasites, e.g., rusts and smuts. The mycelium is branched and septate. The asexual spores are generally not found, but vegetative reproduction by fragmentation is common. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions. Transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma of a different plant

125869.sol: Geitonogamy – Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant. Xenogamy – Transfer of pollen grains from anther to the stigma of a different plant. This is the only type of pollination which during pollination brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma.

127417.sol: Cryopreservation is an advanced ex-situ conservation technique where gametes of threatened species are preserved in viable and fertile conditions at very low temperatures ( -196^ C in liquid nitrogen). Sacred groves are tracts of forest set aside for in-situ protection, often associated with religious and cultural traditions. Biodiversity hotspots are regions identified for maximum in-situ conservation due to their high levels of species richness and high degree of endemism. Zoological parks are ex-situ conservatio

127470.text: In which of the following both pairs have correct combination?
options: In-situ conservation Ex-situ conservation National Park Botanical gardens
In-situ conservation Ex-situ conservation Cryopreservation Wildlife sanctuaries
In-situ conservation Ex-situ conservation Seed bank National Park
In-situ conservation Ex-situ conservation Tissue culture Wildlife sanctuaries
127470.sol: In-situ conservation is the conservation of resources in its natural habitat. Examples of In-situ conservation are national parks, biosphere reserve, parks and sanctuaries. Ex-situ conservation is the conservation of resources outside its habitat may be in the wild area or within human care. The examples are botanical gardens, seed bank, gene bank, etc.

127481.subject: Botany
127481.text: Which one of the following areas in India, is a hot spot of biodiversity?
127481.sol: Hot spots are areas that are extremely rich in species diversity, have high endemism and are under constant threat. In India, two hot spots are found extending into neighbouring countries. The Western Ghats/Sri Lanka and the Indo-Burman region (covering the Eastern Himalayas also known as cradle of speciation).

127561.subject: Botany
127561.text: What is the purpose of studying the ecosystem?
options: To understand the relationships within it
To appreciate its input and output
127561.sol: The purpose of studying the ecosystem is to understand the relationships within it, appreciate its input and output, and comprehend the energy flows. We will first look at the structure of the ecosystem, in order to appreciate the input (productivity), transfer of energy (food chain/web, nutrient cycling) and the output (degradation and energy loss). We will also look at the relationships – cycles, chains, webs – that are created as a result of these energy flows within the system and their inter- relationship .

128150.sol: Tendon is an example of dense regular connective tissue. Skin contains dense irregular connective tissue, where fibroblasts and fibres are oriented differently. Bone is a type of specialised connective tissue. Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue located beneath the skin. Therefore, the correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III. Stellar distances are measured in kilometres. 3. When we see stars we apparently are peeping into the past 4. The origin of life is considered a unique event in the history of universe.
132825.sol: When we look at stars on a clear night sky we are, in a way, looking back in time. Stellar distances are measured in light years. 135336.sol: Calotropis produces highly poisonous cardiac glycosides as a chemical defence against herbivores. Acacia possesses thorns as a morphological means of defence. 135401.sol: The equation dN dt = rN describes the exponential (geometric) growth model where resources are unlimited. The equation dN dt = rN ( K-N K ) describes the Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth model where resources are limited. In these equations, K represents the carrying capacity of the habitat, which is the maximum number of individuals the environment can support. N represents the population density at time t . Endarch condition is seen in stem whereas exarch condition is found in roots of all vascular plants.

95783.subject: Botany
95783.text: Reproduction in bacteria is shown in following diagram. Select the correct match.
options: Mode of Reproduction Conditions Budding Favourable
Mode of Reproduction Conditions Binary fission Favourable
Mode of Reproduction Conditions Spore formation Unfavourable
Mode of Reproduction Conditions Budding Unfavourable
95783.sol: Reproduction: Mainly by fission (during favorable conditions). These also reproduce by spore formation (during unfavorable conditions) or by primitive type of DNA transfer from one bacteria to another. Heterotrophs are most abundant in nature. These also play important role in curdling of milk, production of antibiotics, nitrogen fixation in legumes, etc.

96010.subject: Botany
96010.text: Read the following statements: (i) Presence of DNA. (ii) Presence of cristae. (iii) Presence of the 70S ribosome. (iv) Enzyme for carbohydrate synthesis. (v) Site for oxidative phosphorylation. How many of the above statements are in common for mitochondria and chloroplast?
96010.sol: Mitochondria and chloroplast both have their own DNA and ribosomes, and are self-replicating. They both have a double membrane.

96669.subject: Botany
96669.text: Which of the following is not an insectivorous plant?
96669.sol: Monotropa is a saprophytic plant, whereas Nepenthes, Sarracenia, Drosera, Dionaea, and Utricularia are insectivorous plants.

97119.subject: Botany
97119.text: In guava, cucumber, and ray florets of sunflower, the ovary is
97119.sol: The flowers may be categorized as hypogynous, perigynous, and epigynous depending on the position of calyx, corolla, and androecium with respect to the ovary on the thalamus. When the ovaries are attached above the floral parts or when the gynoecium is at the highest position in a flower, it is known as superior ovary, eg: mustard and brinjal. When the ovary lies below the floral parts and the flower rises above the ovary it is known as inferior ovary, eg: in flowers of guava, cucumber, and ray florets of sunflower

97337.subject: Botany
97337.text: The cut flowers and vegetables can be kept fresh for a long period with the help of:
97337.sol: Cytokinin is a growth promoter and delays the process of senescence by promoting nutrient mobilization. This delay in senescence by cytokinin is also called as Richmond Lang effect.

97347.subject: Botany
97347.sol: The phenomenon where the later stems are suppressed in growth by the growth of the central stem is referred to as apical dominance. This occurs at the shoot tip due to the production of plant hormones. Plant hormones are chemicals that regulate the growth and development of the plant. The hormone that induces apical dominance is auxins and the hormone that break apical dominance is cytokinin.

97363.subject: Botany
97363.text: The cell-derived from meristems differentiates and regain the capacity to divide by a phenomenon called
97363.sol: The cells derived from root apical and shoot-apical meristems and cambium differentiate and mature to perform specific functions. This act leading to maturation is termed as differentiation. The living differentiated cells, that by now have lost the capacity to divide can regain the capacity of division under certain conditions. This phenomenon is termed as dedifferentiation. While doing so, such meristems/tissues are able to divide and produce cells that once again lose the capacity to divide but mature to perform

97467.subject: Botany
97467.text: In which group of plant kingdom gametophyte is depend on sporophyte?
97467.sol: In gymnosperm main plant body is diploid sporophyte which produces small gametophyte which is not free living and independent structure and is dependent on sporophyte for development and nutrition. Male gametophyte is pollen grain which is liberated after its germination and female gametophyte is endosperm which remain on sporophyte before and after fertilization.

97938.subject: Botany
97938.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Different substances move independently along their concentration gradient in mass flow.
Active absorption of ions from the soil by the root is mainly affected by respiratory activity of root.
The translocation of organic solutes in sieve tube members is supported by mass flow.
Root pressure develops due to active absorption.
97938.sol: Mass or bulk flow is the movement of substances in bulk from source to sink as a result of pressure differences. Mass flow is not to be confused with diffusion which depends on concentration gradients within a medium rather than pressure gradients of the medium itself.

6a7a1ff8101e50bde4d63d75.text: A block of ice of mass 150 g at 0^ C is dropped into 250 g of water at T^ C . It is observed that exactly 100 g of ice melts by the time the mixture reaches thermal equilibrium. The value of T is ________. [Use: Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg ⁻¹ K ⁻¹ , Latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.36 10^5 J kg ⁻¹ ]
6a7a1ff8101e50bde4d63d75.sol: Since only a part of the ice melts ( 100 g out of 150 g ), the final temperature of the mixture must be 0^ C . According to the principle of calorimetry, the heat lost by the water equals the heat gained by the melting ice. Heat lost by water: Q₁ = m_w s_w T Q₁ = 0.25 4200 (T - 0) = 1050 T J Heat gained by ice to melt 100 g : Q₂ = m_ melt L Q₂ = 0.1 3.36 10^5 = 33600 J Equating the heat lost and heat gained: 1050 T = 33600 T = 33600 1050 = 32 The initial temperature of the water was 32^ C . Answer: 32
